feedback.problem:
Given that the expression $2(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x)$ can be written as $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ)$ with ${0}^{∘}<ϕ<{90}^{∘}$ and $R>0$, what is the value of $ϕ?$

$ϕ=$ 
{{field-1}}${}^{∘}$
feedback.worked_solution:
The sum formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡x+R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
2(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
2(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x)=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡x+(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=2 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=2\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\sqrt{3} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\sqrt{3}) \\ ϕ & =60\,{\,}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
